chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who accused his wife of adultery, so they performed li'an (mutual cursing), then he accused her again after they had separated, also of adultery. Is there a hadd (fixed penalty) upon him? He said: Yes, there is a hadd upon him.

key_terms.قَذَفَ: Accused of adultery (specifically for the hadd penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who accuses his wife of adultery, performs li'an, and then accuses her again after separation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the hadd penalty for qadhf (false accusation of adultery) remains applicable even if the husband re-accuses his wife after the li'an ceremony has already dissolved the marriage. It highlights the distinct legal nature of the post-li'an accusation, distinguishing it from the initial claim that triggered the mutual cursing procedure. This ruling underscores the permanence of the hadd liability once the condition of false accusation is established, regardless of subsequent marital status changes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about a man who accused his wife, so he cursed, then accused her after the separation as well, with the adultery, is there a Penalty (Hadd) upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, upon him is the Penalty (Hadd)’.
